import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

Read the lead's report (no frontmatter, no external URLs). Checking a published sibling report for conventions, then I'll write the canonical file.

Writing the canonical `apollo_tui_startup_slowness.md` now: research query, infographic, bottom line, then the analysis, ending with the ranked changes.

Validating anchors with pandoc and diffing word-for-word against the lead's report to confirm nothing was dropped.

Anchors all resolve. Now the word-level diff against the original to catch any dropped content.

The deletions shown are relocations (the evidence base and machine profile moved). Confirming with a word-count multiset check that no original word is missing:

Only section numbers, heading punctuation, and link-inserted punctuation differ. One restore: the old heading's "on apollo" got dropped, so I'm putting it back in the setup line.

Registered. Now the final declaration.

I published the lead's report as the canonical file `202610/apollo_tui_startup_slowness/apollo_tui_startup_slowness.md` in the research repo and registered it as `research:202610/apollo_tui_startup_slowness/apollo_tui_startup_slowness.md` (`file:explicit:bf97623915b7e265c6311a70`). The research repo commit is declared; the host makes it after this turn ends.

**How the file opens:** title, then a one-blockquote research query, then the infographic (`apollo_tui_startup_slowness_infographic.png`, which exists beside the report), then `## Bottom line`. The lead's report had no frontmatter, so there was none to keep.

**How I reorganized it:** the sections now run telemetry → mechanism → machine profile → the lead's experiment → disagreements resolved → scope and evidence base → how to re-measure → ranked changes. I kept the ranked list last because the request asked for the analysis to end with it.
- **Heading numbers removed:** pandoc adds numbers to the PDF on its own. Headings that are link targets now use only letters, digits, spaces and hyphens.
- **Section references turned into links:** "§8" and "§4.5" were the lead's numbers, so they are now links to the matching sections.
- **New in-document links:** I added a few, from the bottom-line points and some ranked items to the sections that back them.
- **Wording:** apart from section headings, wording is the lead's. The only other changes are these new link phrases, the setup-line rewording below and the research-query summary.

**Checks:**
- **Nothing dropped:** a word-count comparison against `__final.md` shows every claim, number, table, caveat and code reference made it over. The only differences are the removed section numbers, reworded headings, and punctuation moved to make room for links.
- **One fix after that check:** the lead's experiment heading had said "on apollo". The new heading lost that, so I put "on apollo" back in the setup line ("In the lead's A/B on apollo").
- **Links:** pandoc parses the file, and all 10 in-document anchors match a real heading.
- **External URLs:** the lead's report had none, so nothing needed checking and nothing was marked unrepairable.

I did not modify `__final.md` or any of the drafts.
